answer: An honest AI agent must invest 1 unit of verified labor to complete a task, while 1,000 fakes must incur 1,000 units, ensuring work remains non-amortizable. The verifier monitors an operational canyon of task sequences to block replay, scanning each ridge of the state transition graph for duplicate proofs. If an audit uncovers a signature of replayed work, it acts as an anchor for identity revocation without refund. This protocol assumes that tasks are atomic and non-shareable, preventing parallel fake identities from claiming a single unit of work.
